based_on: ASD-STE100 Simplified Technical English, Issue 9 — structure: writing rules + controlled dictionary + a technical-name allowance
Federal Plain Language Guidelines (2011) and the plainlanguage.gov word-substitution list — both US government work, public domain
ISO 24495-1:2023 Plain language, Part 1 — the four principles
Wydick, Plain English for Lawyers — base verbs, surplus words

corpora.name: simplewiki
corpora.register: Simple English Wikipedia — plain English by construction

corpora.name: explain
corpora.register: plain explanation written for a lay reader (ELI5)

dictionary.used_for: direct headword recognition, inflections, and Wikipedia frequency rank

provenance.register_lift: geometric mean of (federal bill rate / prose rate) and (California bill rate / prose rate), Jeffreys-smoothed; prose = mean of all seven prose corpora
provenance.doc_spread: share of federal bills containing the word
provenance.grading: grades are editorial judgement, seeded from the plainlanguage.gov list. The register statistics rank candidates for review; they do not decide grades.
provenance.caveat: Corpus samples are the first N documents or tokens of the revision-pinned streaming datasets above; cache digests identify the exact aggregate counts this build used.

tier_rules.core: (any modern corpus >= 10.0/M) or (gutenberg >= 10.0/M and modern >= 1.0/M); attested >= 1.0/M in 2 of 7 prose corpora or wiki rank <= 30000; plus attested inflections
tier_rules.open: known to OpenGloss and >= 0.5/M in a prose corpus
tier_rules.recognized: OpenGloss headword below the corpus thresholds; review technical or restricted uses
tier_rules.recognized_phrase: exact multiword OpenGloss headword; available to --explain, not an approval
tier_rules.unlisted: not in the corpus tiers or OpenGloss; review as a domain term, coined form, name, or possible error
tier_rules.sensitive: curated never_core list, demoted out of both tiers so a first use is deliberate

register_markers: in spite of the fact that

phrase_substitutions.from: in spite of the fact that

phrase_substitutions.source: Wydick; measured no more bureaucratic than general prose, but still three words for one
